summary: Juasa A Jan–May 2026 yield 4.88 t/ha vs 6.14 a year earlier (-20.5%); Agro blames crop dilution from newly harvested P23U and doubts the P22T3 figure.
Juasa A+B Jan–Jun 2026 (PA): 14,032 t FFB, 6.53 t/ha vs 8.79 budget (-26%); cost RM324.69/t (A+B costs); OER 16.38% vs 18.94% budget.
2025 full-year yield was 17.42 t/ha, up from 17.01 in 2024 (Agro graph); Juasa B was 9.73.
Short of 3 harvesters and 12 sprayers (Jun 2026); sprayer output 3.5 ha/man-day and earnings below basic wage; assistant-in-charge post vacant.
21% of area (316.95 ha) flood-prone; no drain desilting to June; 2026 replant (234.70 ha) felled, not yet planted; manuring 73% to May.

issues.title: PA says yield 3% below last year; it is 9% below
issues.detail: PA 2/2026 para 8.2 says Jan–Jun 2026 yield was 3% below the same period 2025 (7.20 t/ha). 6.53 vs 7.20 t/ha is 9.3% lower, and FFB fell 10.4% (14,032.23 t vs 15,660.18 t). Figures are Juasa A+B combined.

issues.title: PA cost of production budget column does not reconcile
issues.detail: PA section 9 shows estimate to date general charges RM13.90/t, upkeep 146.76, harvesting 118.49 (total 279.15). The PA tables imply about RM103/t general charges (RM1,950,318 / 18,899 t), RM109/t upkeep and RM87.97/t harvesting. Actual column does reconcile (RM96.00, 136.85, 91.83 per t). Budget cost per tonne left blank.

issues.title: Circle and selective spraying: text vs table
issues.detail: PA 6.3.1 says 1,597.28 ha (82% of 1,955.75 ha) circle sprayed; its table shows 2,677.83 ha of 3,150.73 ha (85%). PA 6.4.1 says 1,859.88 ha (72% of 2,596.66 ha) selective; table shows 2,799.38 ha of 3,536.18 ha (79%). Dashboard uses the table figures.

issues.title: Harvesting rounds do not match 14-day interval
issues.detail: PA 7.3 says 9.4 rounds in Jan–Jun 2026 (about 19 days per round) against 12 budgeted, but PA 7.4 says the interval averaged 14 days. Agro Table 9 shows 10–19 days in Juasa A, Jan–May 2026.

issues.title: Labour required total does not add up
issues.detail: PA labour table (Jun 2026) lists required 46+5+26+4+0+0+22 = 103 but prints total required 108 with variance -10 (93 actual). Variance of -10 matches 103.

issues.title: Manuring: PA says 8 of 8 rounds done, Agro says 73%
issues.detail: PA 6.5.1.1 says manuring completed to June at 8 rounds against 8 budgeted. Agro Table 7 says Juasa A completed 73% (521.65 of 713.10 mt) to May, with RP only 43% and Compound A 50%.

issues.title: PA fertiliser doses differ from Agro programme
issues.detail: PA manuring tables show P22T3 Mix B 2.00 kg in Jul and Oct, PR23U Comp B 2.00 kg in Apr, Aug and Oct, PR24V Comp A 2.00 kg and RP 2.00 kg. Agro Appendix 1a (amended 2026) shows 1.50, 1.20, 1.00 and 1.75 kg respectively. PA also labels P01K columns Mix B/NK2/RP differently from the Agro programme.

issues.title: Rat damage: PA census vs Agro and PA total
issues.detail: PA rat census shows 17–33% damage per sub-block but prints a total of 12%. Agro Table 13 (Q1 2026) shows P19A 13%, P20R 17%, P21S 21%, P01K 11% for the same blocks. Both are above the 10% threshold.

issues.title: Pruning status: PA 64% vs Agro about 90%
issues.detail: PA 6.6.1 says 64% of the 5,046.84 ha programme was pruned and calls progress slow. Agro Table 10 shows 90–91% complete for Juasa A rounds 1–5, but it counts P97H (8.1 ha) and P13M (4 ha) as done in its area column while their percentage is 0%.

issues.title: Palm stand figures inconsistent
issues.detail: Agro Table 4 gives 148 SPH for P19A to PN25W, but the PA rat census sheet shows 125–142 SPH for P19–P22 sub-blocks (for example A1 139, S2 125). Agro P92C 9,553 palms over 77.9 ha is 123 SPH, not the 135 shown as current; P01K 18,545 palms over 164.2 ha is 113, not 123.

issues.title: Last-year crop column looks too high
issues.detail: PA section 8 shows last-year column 40,080 t FFB and 18.42 t/ha for Juasa A+B on 2,175.54 ha. Agro gives 2025 yields of 17.42 t/ha (Juasa A) and 9.73 t/ha (Juasa B), so a combined figure above both is not possible if that column is 2025 actual.

issues.title: Flooded area percentage wrong in Agro Appendix 3a
issues.detail: Agro Appendix 3a lists 316.95 ha flooded and prints 45% of 1,146.14 ha. The listed sub-blocks add up to 980.85 ha (32%); the text (4.4) says 21% of 1,537.34 ha. Appendix 3b prints 60% for Juasa B against 40% in the text.

issues.title: Replant felling dates differ
issues.detail: PA says felling and chipping started and completed in June (comment column) or started June and completed July (10.4.1). Agro Table 15 for the 24–25 June visit shows felling 95% in progress, and its text refers to works on 10–11 July 2026, after the visit date.

issues.title: P22T3 yield drop doubtful
issues.detail: Agro Table 16 shows P22T3 falling from 16.90 to 2.65 t/ha Jan–May (-14.25); Agro itself says the figure is doubtful. It also says Juasa B 2025 harvest intervals ranged 9–108 days, likely a typo.

actions.item: Recruit harvesters (short 3) and sprayers (short 12, critical)
Replace Mr Tomi with an Estate Manager or Assistant in charge
Train sprayers (3.5 ha/man-day, earnings below basic wage); verify pumps and chemical records; drop Ally from circle spraying
Speed up progressive pruning (64% to June); fix P21 basal pruning and under-pruning
Raise harvester productivity and working hours to cut turnover
Complete supplying in PR23 (846 palms to date) by end 2026; census and supply PR24
Finish palm census (P93D1, D2, P97H6, P01K3, P13M) and census P20R–P25W; infill towards 148 SPH
Ganoderma census before replanting; apply SOP where infection exceeds 10%
Resume drain desilting (none done to May/June); prepare DEM and water level plan, keep water table 50–80 cm
Apply EFB uniformly, 1 ft from palm base, outside circles; map unsuitable areas
Apply fertiliser in full circles; pallets for all bags; spread frond stacking method
Improve sub-surface manuring output (pre-holing, wheelbarrows) at P01K1
Post-baiting rat census; quarterly census; baiting where damage exceeds 10%
Repair or replace 23 of 84 barn owl boxes; T-perches in young areas
Cost comparison of Alika ZC vs cypermethrin for rhinoceros beetle in PR24 V2
Remove runt palms (P21S in progress); finish epiphyte poisoning in P11M, P01K1, P01K2
Stop overnight bunches (P19A3, P23U1); mound leaning palms in P21S3 and P22T3
Replant 2026: complete roads, drains, camber bunds, lateriting; mark peat areas, install piezometers, consider 160 SPH on peat
Re-establish Mucuna in P23U and P25W2–W3
Nursery: stringent culling, correct CRF method (50 g in two holes) or Sumi/Fuji Coat
Verify P22T3 Jan–May yield (16.90 vs 2.65 t/ha)
Felling and chipping of 234.70 ha 2026 replant completed

kb:
LADANG JUASA A, Fleet Properties Sdn Bhd (Prosper group). Fact pack drawn from two reports: PA Report 2/2026 (Planting Advisor Mr. Boey Chee Weng, visit 27 July 2026, reviewing January to June 2026) and Agronomy Report 1/2026, Juasa A and B combined report, Visit for 1-2026 (Senior Agronomist Mr. Lai Hong Heng, visit 24 and 25 June 2026; previous agronomy visit 8 January 2026; 2026 manuring programme). Management: General Manager Mr Lee Chong Yew; Mr Chan Wah Vee is called Senior Manager in the PA (directly managing Juasa A) and Estate Manager in the Agro, which also names En. Mohd Shafirun Bin Mohd Azba as Senior Manager. Assistant in charge Mr Tomi Hendra joined the estate 5 March 2026 and resigned from June 2026; no replacement yet.

IMPORTANT: several PA figures cover Juasa A and Juasa B combined (general charges, upkeep, harvesting costs, crop, yield, cost of production, vehicle running). These are labelled A+B below. Agro Tables 16 give Juasa A alone.

AREA (PA 2/2026, Section 2, hectares): Mature 841.14 (P92 C3-4 77.94; P93 D3-6 174.80; P01 K1-2 70.70; P11M 27.00; P19 A1-3 171.40; P20 R1-3 128.30; P21 S1-3 150.60; P22 T3 40.40). Immature 461.50 (PN23 U1-4 190.25; PN24 V1-2 113.70; PR25 W1-3 157.55). Replanting 234.70 (PR26 X1-3, being P93 D1-D2, P97 H6, P01 K3, P13M). Plantable ravine 4.90. Unplantable: office/housing 1.62, mill 15.31, nursery 23.17, other 2.69. Total estate 1,585.03 ha. Agro Table 1 total planted 1,537.34 ha in 13 main blocks and 33 sub-blocks. Agro age profile (Table 3, Juasa A, ha): 0-3 years 461.5 (30%); 4-7 years 490.7 (32%); 8-19 years 31 (2%); 20-25 years 164.2 (11%); over 26 years 389.94 (25%). Replanting 2026 on 234.7 ha (P97H6, P93D1, P93D2, P01K3, P13M); P92C3-4 tentatively 2027. Combined A and B only 9.92% prime-age (8-19 years) vs ideal 48%. Flood-prone area in Juasa A 316.95 ha (21%) vs Juasa B 613.90 ha (40%) (Agro 4.4, 8.4). PA: mature areas were not changed in 2026; PR22 (P22T3) declared mature January 2026.

PALM STAND (Agro 2.3, Table 4): Juasa A 212,019 palms, average 138 SPH (census still in progress, started May 2026 for P93D1, P93D2, P97H6, P01K3, P13M). Agro lists P19A to PN25W at 148 SPH, P92C 135 (previous 123), P93D 126, P97H 123, P01K 123, P11M/13M 131. Target stand 148 SPH. No palm supplying in Juasa A in 2025.

CROP AND YIELD (PA 2/2026 Section 8, Juasa A+B combined, hectarage used 2,149.17 ha, January to June 2026): FFB 14,032.23 t vs budget to date 18,899 t, annual budget 37,446 t, same period 2025 15,660.18 t. CPO 2,298.64 t vs 3,579 t budget; kernel 701.12 t. Extraction CPO 16.38% vs 18.94% budget (16.83% same period 2025); kernel 5.00%. Yield FFB 6.53 t/ha vs budget 8.79 (26% below); annual budget 17.42; same period 2025 7.20 t/ha. CPO 1.07 t/ha vs 1.67 budget. PA says yield was 3% below 2025 same period; the figures (6.53 vs 7.20) show 9.3% lower. Causes per PA: shortage of harvesters, flooding and low cropping period early in the year. Good fruit sets at P19, P20, P22.
AGRO (Juasa A alone, FFB t/ha, Table 16, January to May 2026 vs January to May 2025): estate total 4.88 vs 6.14 (-1.26, -20.52%) over 1,266.09 ha. Agro says the decline is more likely crop dilution from newly harvested P23U. P22T3 16.90 to 2.65 is doubtful. Block yields 2026 (2025): C3 7.91 (6.78); C4 4.24 (5.60); D1 4.13 (5.17); D2 3.89 (4.72); D3 6.83 (6.74); D4 6.68 (7.78); D5 5.74 (6.63); D6 5.52 (8.17); H6 4.32 (6.34); K1 7.77 (7.19); K2 5.67 (7.17); K3 3.23 (1.75); 11M 9.38 (9.29); 13M 6.76 (4.79); A1 5.99 (9.58); A2 6.18 (7.53); A3 8.29 (9.70); R1 7.57 (8.72); R2 7.87 (9.42); R3 8.63 (8.71); S1 2.45 (2.03); S2 3.11 (2.08); S3 4.54 (3.61); T3 2.65 (16.90); U1 0.43 (0.00); U2 0.39 (0.00); U3 0.49 (0.00); U4 1.66 (0.00). Juasa B for comparison 3.87 vs 4.00. Annual FFB yield Juasa A (Agro graph, section 8.1): 2021 17.58; 2022 11.15; 2023 12.72; 2024 17.01; 2025 17.42 t/ha; Juasa B 2025 9.73. PR23 scout harvesting since January 2026: 0.96 t/ha to June (PA 10.1.10).

COST OF PRODUCTION (PA Section 9, Juasa A+B costs, January to June 2026): RM324.69 per t FFB (RM1,982.07 per t CPO). General charges RM96.00; upkeep and cultivation RM136.85; harvesting and collection RM91.83 per t. The PA budget columns (estimate to date RM279.15 total, general charges RM13.90, upkeep RM146.76, harvesting RM118.49; annual budget RM808.46) do not reconcile with the PA RM tables, so no budget cost per tonne is quoted. PA says cost was high because crop was below budget.
GENERAL CHARGES (PA Section 5, A+B): RM1,347,116.32 actual vs RM1,950,318 budget to date (underspent 31%), annual budget RM3,900,590. Management and supervision RM869,973.84; labour and amenities RM242,535.25; other RM234,607.23. RM438.86 per ha vs RM635.38.
UPKEEP, MATURE (PA Section 6, A+B): RM1,920,326 vs RM2,059,350 to date (underspent 7%); RM893.50 per ha vs RM958.21. RM per ha actual vs budget: weeding 103.16 vs 128.98; manuring 666.63 vs 603.30; pest and disease 13.89 vs 19.30; census 0.00 vs 1.95; drains 28.35 vs 86.86; roads 43.27 vs 34.23; culverts and bridges 5.36 vs 5.63; soil and water conservation 0.53 vs 17.82; boundary 0.52 vs 0; tools 0.15; pruning 31.64 vs 60.14.
HARVESTING AND COLLECTION (PA Section 7, A+B): RM1,288,620 vs RM1,662,708 budget to date; RM91.83 per t vs RM87.97 (annual budget RM88.80). Labour RM67.35, internal transport RM19.14, incentive RM0.59, top-up wages RM4.75 per t. PA notes budget was spread evenly over 12 months, so cost comparison is not meaningful. Rounds 9.4 vs 12 budgeted; interval averaged 14 days; outturn 89%. 4 Badang units (3 cutters and 2 collectors each); 4 cutters and 1 collector advised when harvesters are adequate. Harvesting rates and output (t/man-day, earnings RM/day, basic wage RM65.39): P92 C3-4 2.18, RM113.36; P93 D 1.39, RM66.72; P97 H6 1.56, RM70.20; P01 K1 1.72, RM65.36; P01 K2-3 1.51, RM61.91; P11M 1.93, RM63.69; P13M 0.75, RM27.75; P19 1.48, RM100.64; P20 1.61, RM117.53; P21 1.18, RM97.94; P22 T3 0.85, RM74.80; PN23 0.43, RM38.27. Productivity still low; PA wants longer working hours to lift wages and cut turnover.

LABOUR (PA Section 3, June 2026): harvesters 43 vs 46 required (short 3; ratio 1:24 ha). Weeding and spraying 14 vs 26 (short 12, critical). Manuring 9 vs 4. Drivers and loaders 5 vs 5. Other 22 vs 22. Total 93 vs 108 as printed (the categories add up to 103 required, and the printed variance is -10). Ratio workers to planted ha 1:17; ideal 1:13 because of immature and replant areas. Staff numerically adequate.

WEEDING (PA 6.3 and 6.4): circle spraying table 2,677.83 ha done of 3,150.73 ha programme (85%) while text says 1,597.28 ha (1.5 rounds) or 82% of 1,955.75 ha. Output 3.5 ha/man-day, rate RM15 per ha, earnings RM52.56 per day (below basic RM65.38); glyphosate 0.67 kg/ha and Ally 0.04 kg/ha (7 pumps per ha) judged too high; Ally not needed for circles; assistants cannot verify pumps per man-day. Selective spraying table 2,799.38 ha of 3,536.18 ha (79%); text 1,859.88 ha (1.7 rounds) or 72% of 2,596.66 ha. Mist blower 3.5 ha/man-day, RM16 per ha, earnings RM56 per day, only 4.6 hours worked; potential 11 pumps per man-day vs 7 achieved. Circles and inter-rows generally clean; Giant Paspalum, VOPs and woodies in P21S. Agro (Tables 11, to May 2026): inter-row round 1 83%, round 2 66%; circle round 1 83%, round 2 18%. Spraying stopped in blocks to be replanted (P93D1, D2, P97H, P01K3, P13M). Agro: ground vegetation improved on 2-2025 visit, soft grasses dominant; localized dense weeds in P21S3, P20R2, P19A3, P23U4, P21S1; localized blanket over-spraying in P20R2 should not be routine; narrow path spraying acceptable; keep 3 to 4 ft radius clean circle. Immature: PR23 circle 2 of 2 rounds, selective 42%; PR24 circle and selective 67%; PR25 100%.

MANURING (Agro Section 4, Table 7, to May 2026): Juasa A completed 73% of programme: 521.65 of 713.10 MT (delivered 571.35 MT). Mixture B 298.65 of 332.10 MT (90%); NK2 59.70 of 59.70 (100%); RP 94.15 of 220.00 (43%); Compound A 16.85 of 33.70 (50%); Compound B 52.30 of 67.60 (77%). Juasa B only 39%. PA 6.5.1: manuring completed to June at 8 rounds against 8 budgeted; broadcasting 30 bags/man-day, RM2.30 per bag, RM69 per day (satisfactory). Sub-surface at P01K1 0.5 ha/man-day, 9 bags per day, RM25.20 per day; benchmark 1 ha and 20 bags; pre-holing and wheelbarrows advised. PA saw fertiliser applied in half circles only; supervision must improve. Agro: application quality acceptable in P19A2; fertiliser mostly on pallets but small portion on floor; frond stacking method begun, not consistent. Wet season rainfall tends to be heavy at year end so first half programme should be completed quickly; manure young mature and prime-age palms first.
EFB: 2025 Juasa A 19,181.6 MT over 475.86 ha (40 MT/ha, 99% of 479.54 ha). 2026 to May 2,059 MT over 51.48 ha (P93D4 and P24V2). PA: 108.65 ha of 511.15 ha budgeted applied from May at 40 t/ha; tractors 67 t/day, RM2 per t. Agro: EFB uneven and scattered in P19A2; placed too close to palms in P25W2, P23U3; inside circles in P23U2; keep about 1 ft from palm base; PA wants 3 rings per palm at PR25. Mapping of unsuitable areas needed.
2026 FERTILISER PROGRAMME (Agro Appendix 1a, kg per palm): P93 D3-D6 NK2 2.50 (Mar); P01K1 Mix B 8 subsurface (Jan, marked *) and RP 1.50 (May); P01K2 NK2 2.00 (Feb) and RP 1.75 (May); P11M Mix B 2.25, 2.25, RP 1.75, Mix B 1.50, 1.50; P19A1 Mix B 2.25 (Jan), 2.00 (Apr), RP 2.00, Mix B 1.50, 1.50; P19A2-A3 and P20R Mix B 2.00, 2.00, RP 2.00, Mix B 1.50, 1.50; P21S Mix B 1.75, 1.75, RP 2.00, 1.25, 1.50; PR22/T3 Mix B 1.50, 1.50, RP 2.00, 1.50, 1.50; PR23/U Comp B 1.20 four rounds and RP 2.00; PR24/V Comp A 1.00 three rounds and RP 1.75; PR25/W CRF 600 g and RP 500 g in the planting hole, then Comp 0.80 (Aug), RP 1.50 (Sep), Comp 0.90 (Nov). No manuring for blocks replanted in 2026 or 2027. The PA manuring table shows higher doses for P22T3 (2.00 in Jul and Oct), PR23U (2.00 in Apr, Aug, Oct) and PR24V (2.00) than Agro Appendix 1a. New planting or supply: 600 g CRF and 500 g RP in the hole; then none up to 9 months. FY2026 programme must not carry past January 2027.

PRUNING (PA 6.6, Agro 6.2): PA progressive pruning 3,251.26 ha or 64% of 5,046.84 ha programme; slow because harvesters pruned slowly and are short. Cost per ha per year: P92/P93 RM140; P01 RM120; P11 RM85; P19/P20 RM70; P21/P22 RM60. Basal pruning missed and under-pruned palms in P21. Agro Table 10 shows about 90 to 91 percent of rounds complete (P92C 4th and 5th rounds only 52%; P01K 43%; P97H and P13M 0%). Agro: young mature pruning acceptable, retain at least two fronds under lowest bunch; dry hanging fronds in P93D3, D4, D5, D6, P01K1-2, P11M. Runt palm marking and removal started in P21S; epiphyte poisoning started May 2026 in P11M, P01K1, P01K2 (Garlon and diesel 1:10).

PESTS (PA 6.7, Agro 6.5): PA rat census (300 palms per sub-block): K1 25%, K2 26%, 11M 24%, A1 26%, A2 30%, A3 33%, R1 29%, R2 26%, R3 17%, S1 21%, S2 26%, S3 22%, T3 19%; table total printed as 12%; damage very extensive. Baiting (RM5 per ha per round): 588.40 ha, round 1 100%, round 2 66% bait take, round 3 33%, round 4 11%; 3 rounds in P21, P11M and 4 rounds in P19, P20, P01. Threshold 10%; census every 3 months. Agro Table 13 (Q1 2026): P01K 11%, P11M 18%, P19A 13%, P20R 17%, P21S 21%, P22T 16%. Estate stopped baiting when bait uptake fell below 30%; no post-baiting census. Barn owl boxes 84, 73% occupied (January 2026), 23 boxes (27%) in poor condition. T-perches suggested for PR23 and young palms. Rhinoceros beetle: PR24 V2 significant damage; cypermethrin monthly; try Alika ZC 30 ml per 16 L at 3-week intervals. Ganoderma census not yet done in Juasa A; needed before replanting (SOP if infection over 10%).

HARVESTING QUALITY (Agro 6.1): interval January to May 2026 Juasa A 10 to 19 days (2025: 10 to 20). Overripe in fresh bunches P20R 4%, P19A3 8% (acceptable). Overnight bunches left in P19A3 and harvested FFB left overnight in P23U1. Substantial leaning palms in P21S3 and P22T3 (mounding advised). Juasa A much cleaner for loose fruit than Juasa B.

DRAINAGE: Juasa A de-silted 2,087.70 chains in 2025; none to May 2026 (PA: none to June because all excavators were used for felling and chipping at the 2026 replant). Budget 160 chains 8x6x4 ft, 100 chains 12x8x6, 50 chains canal not done. Roads: 515.43 of 600 chains graded (RM19 per chain); 1,395 chains laterite not done; road conditions satisfactory. Water table target 50 to 80 cm below surface; DEM map and water level plan advised; UMB water management team may advise on flooding (group MD comment). Average rainfall 2,827 mm per year, about 12 rainy days per month, 19.6 mm per rainy day; June average about 153 mm (Agro). Year by year rainfall is not given in these reports.

IMMATURE AND REPLANT (PA Section 10, Agro Section 7): PR23 U1-U4 190.25 ha: many vacant points from flooding, 846 palms supplied to date, declare mature 2027, basal pruning done Dec 2025, manuring 3 of 3 rounds, Mucuna sparse in P23U. PR24 V1-V2 113.70 ha: no supplying done yet; census needed; palms bearing sporadic bunches. PR25 W1-W3 157.55 ha: planting completed February 2026, advanced planting material, Mucuna mortality high in W2 and W3, manuring due August. PR26 (234.70 ha replant): felling and chipping started June and completed July per PA; Agro Table 15 (June) felling 95%, new road 80%, new drain 70%, cambered bund 20%, lateriting nil, planting nil. 120 ha need camber bunds; terraces being rebuilt to 16 ft.

NURSERY (PA Section 11, Agro Section 3): 44,000 Yangambi (ML161) and 5,000 three-way cross seedlings, 8 months old; culling to date 6%; stringent culling needed (many runts). Ekot CRF 75 g per palm caused deficiency, supplementary urea and kieserite given; PA advises Sumi Coat or Fuji Coat 50 g; Agro advises Ekot CRF 50 g in two holes of 25 g.

OTHER: Vehicle running (Hilux, A+B) RM18,803.51 vs budget RM27,336. Capex RM3,600 spent (fibre boat, 19 January 2026) vs RM6,000 budget.

notes: Cost tables (Sections 5, 6, 7, 9) cover Juasa A+B combined; Juasa A and Juasa B PA 2/2026 print identical tables, so both files carry the same figures.
FFB basis: 14,032.23 t actual Jan-Jun 2026; 18,899 t budget to date (Section 8, A+B combined).
General Charges and Upkeep items: report prints RM and RM/ha only, so RM/t = RM / FFB t (actual 14,032.23 t; budget 18,899 t), marked calc. Harvest items are as printed (Section 7).
Sub-items add up to group totals: GC RM1,347,116.32 actual / RM1,950,318 budget; mature upkeep RM1,920,326 / RM2,059,350; harvest 91.83 / 87.97. No mismatch.
Group actuals 96.00 / 136.85 / 91.83 = 324.69 match Section 9 and dashboard costParts.

Section 9 prints a different 'estimate to date' budget: GC 13.90 (appears a misprint; annual 277.97), Upkeep 146.76, Harvest 118.49, total 279.15. These do not reconcile with Sections 5-7 budgets divided by budget FFB (GC 103.20, Upkeep 108.97, Harvest 87.97, total 300.14). Group budgets here use the item-consistent figures (Harvest 87.97 as printed in Section 7, matching dashboard).
Upkeep group covers mature upkeep only (matches the printed RM/t); immature and replanting costs are excluded from cost of production.
